gaps: docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:29-34 does not name the exact SDK version, where its separate environment lives, or how an existing Forge installation gets that environment. The current package has no runtime dependency (pyproject.toml:10), and doctor still checks for a standalone Codex executable (src/forge/doctor.py:63-65).

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:29-31 promises that no Codex process remains after each call but gives no shutdown rule for interruption, a crashed client, or a child that ignores normal termination. Those cases need a falsifiable cleanup criterion.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:37-42 makes trusted project hooks part of the full-access safety boundary but checks only whether the project is trusted. The current doctor runs the hook command itself (src/forge/doctor.py:88-103) and prints trust as a note (src/forge/doctor.py:115-125); the spec does not say how it proves Codex actually loaded and ran the approved deny hook before worker execution.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:38-39 and :105-106 do not define a fail-closed result if the SDK approval-handler replacement cannot be installed or receives an unfamiliar request. The proposed contract test needs to prove an approval request is declined, logged, and cannot execute the requested action.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:45-51 leaves the per-kind settings contract to guesswork: which keys may override the normal Codex stack, how invalid files fail, when settings are reloaded on resume, and whether a kind file may override sandbox or approval policy. The [SDK API](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/sdk/python/docs/api-reference.md) exposes configuration and per-turn policy overrides, so their precedence matters.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:54-61 does not identify the title source for a fix, which has no STORY, or state whether Review, Explore, and Debug are merely naming advice for manually opened threads. Those cases cannot be tested against the stated title format.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:64-74 does not define when the local thread record is durably written or how simultaneous `forge work` calls for one item are serialized. A crash after starting a thread, or two callers resuming the same recorded thread, can lose continuity or run overlapping edits; the current close flow has no worker-running check (src/forge/close.py:39-81).

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:67-69 does not define the baseline for 'commits since the thread's last turn' after a rebase, merge, or amended commit, nor whether untracked files are included in 'uncommitted changes'. The continuation can otherwise omit changes the warm thread has not seen.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:70-81 says an unresumable record starts fresh while a failed or interrupted turn stays resumable, but gives no rule for an unknown terminal state after a lost connection. Starting fresh while the old turn may still be writing conflicts with one worker per item and with review of a settled diff.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:76-79 does not define which event fields are persisted, how duplicate or missing events affect the final status, or how token usage is represented when the SDK omits it. The success measure later depends on those logs (docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:114-121).

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:84-85 does not explicitly bind Grill threads to a read-only sandbox at thread start and turn start, or specify what a failed or interrupted read writes. The current read command checks for changed non-ignored checkout files using a temporary Git index (src/forge/story.py:427-438); 'any file changed' needs an exact boundary and a test for ignored files.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:105-106 specifies unknown fields in stub responses but does not require a real bundled-runtime smoke test of start, name, resume, deny, events, and shutdown. A stub can pass while the shipped SDK and app-server disagree.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:109-110 does not identify the real Forge task, its task scope, or the evidence that ties its first build, second `forge work`, review, CI, and human merge to one thread. Without that proof, criterion 8 can be asserted from a unit test alone.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:114-122 does not define the measurement window, whether legitimate fresh starts and failed rounds enter the continuation denominator, or how missing and zero input-token usage affects the median cache share. The 90% and 80% targets are therefore not reproducible.
contradictions: docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:29-31 says each `forge read` call opens a client and runs one turn, but `forge read --amended` only records the amendment (src/forge/story.py:121-126). Running another turn for that form would violate the one-cold-read flow in docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:165-170.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:40-42 says Forge's deny hook enforces task Scope. The shipped hook checks destructive commands, skipped Git hooks, and merges, with no path-scope check (src/forge/deny.py:17-25, src/forge/deny.py:79-105). Scope is supplied to the reviewer instead (src/forge/review.py:134-151), so the claimed enforcement boundary is false.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:48-51 says a task worktree uses its main repository's settings. Forge sync reads and writes `.codex/config.toml` in the checkout passed to it (src/forge/sync.py:181-184, src/forge/sync.py:246-253); the [Codex configuration loader](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs) also loads project configuration for the thread's working tree. The two copies can differ.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:70-74 says a change to the story's approved part starts a fresh worker. The confirmed v1 contract requires a new human approval when that part changes (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:171-176); a fresh thread must not proceed on the unapproved change.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:87-90 says the plugin is removed from Forge outside history, while its roadmap item still requires hybrid mode, plugin fallback, a lease-held server, turn ledgers, steering, and client upgrade through the old route (plans/roadmap.json:1020-1041). The active roadmap points to this spec and must be reconciled before it can yield a buildable story.
resolutions: SDK pin: openai-codex 0.156.1 in the Forge-managed env ~/.local/share/forge/codex-sdk/openai-codex-0.156.1 (harvested from SDK-SETUP); `forge doctor --fix` creates it; with workers = codex, doctor checks that env and the SDK's bundled codex, not a standalone codex executable.

Shutdown: forge work closes the client in a finally block; the app-server child pid is recorded in the item's thread record; the next forge work (or doctor) terminates a still-running recorded child before starting; criterion: after forge work exits (normally, on error, or on Ctrl-C) no app-server child of it remains.

Trust: with workers = codex, an untrusted project is a FAILING doctor row; doctor still runs the hook health check; Codex's per-hook approval cannot be observed, so doctor prints a note to approve Forge's hooks when Codex asks.

Approvals fail closed: if the deny-all approval handler cannot be installed, forge work refuses before any thread exists; every approval request, known or unknown, is declined and logged; a contract test proves a declined request does not execute.

Per-kind settings files may set only model, model_reasoning_effort and model_verbosity; any sandbox, approval or other key is refused with Next; an invalid file refuses; settings are read on every forge work call, including resume.

Titles: a fix's title is `Fix · <fix name> · <why>`; Build/Fix/Lite/Grill are produced by Forge; Review, Explore and Debug are naming guidance for threads a person opens by hand (documented, not produced or tested).

The thread record is written atomically right after thread start, before the first turn; one forge work per item at a time via an exclusive lock file under .git/forge/threads/; a second caller refuses with Next.

Drift baseline: the thread record stores HEAD at the end of each turn; "what changed" = the diff from that commit to the working tree including untracked files; if that commit is no longer an ancestor of HEAD (rebase, amend), start fresh and say why.

Unknown turn state after a lost connection: interrupt the old turn through the SDK and wait for its terminal state; if it cannot be confirmed, refuse with Next: forge work (never run two turns for one item).

Turn log (per machine, .git/forge/threads/<item>.log, never committed): turn id, kind, status, started/ended, input/cached/output tokens (null when the SDK omits them); duplicate events ignored by turn id; the final status comes only from the SDK's turn-completed event.
Grill threads start and run each turn with the read-only sandbox; a failed or interrupted read writes no notes and records no read.
A real smoke test against the pinned SDK (start, name, resume, deny, events, shutdown) runs when the SDK env exists (locally and in an optional CI job that installs it); stubs cover the rest.

The validating task is WARM's own UNPLUG task, built by a Codex worker; its PR body shows the thread name and the turn log lines proving the build and its fix round used one thread id, then review, CI and the human merge.

Measurement window: every Codex fix round from USE-CODEX's merge to the check date; a fresh start because of drift or a lost thread counts as not continued; failed rounds are excluded; rounds with missing token usage are excluded from the cache median.
`forge read --amended` runs no model turn; only the first read of an artifact opens a Codex client.
The deny hook blocks destructive commands, skipped hooks and merges; it does not enforce Scope — Scope is enforced by review. Fix the wording.
`.codex/config.toml` is committed, so every task worktree has it; Codex reads the project config from the thread's cwd; forge sync writes it in the checkout it runs in.
If the story's approved part changed, forge work refuses until the change is re-approved (it does not start a fresh thread on unapproved text).
The roadmap item FORGE-WARM-1's story and acceptance criteria are rewritten to the re-cut spec (via the roadmap fill path in the same PR).

findings: docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:29-34 does not name the exact SDK version, where its separate environment lives, or how an existing Forge installation gets that environment. The current package has no runtime dependency (pyproject.toml:10), and doctor still checks for a standalone Codex executable (src/forge/doctor.py:63-65).

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:29-31 promises that no Codex process remains after each call but gives no shutdown rule for interruption, a crashed client, or a child that ignores normal termination. Those cases need a falsifiable cleanup criterion.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:37-42 makes trusted project hooks part of the full-access safety boundary but checks only whether the project is trusted. The current doctor runs the hook command itself (src/forge/doctor.py:88-103) and prints trust as a note (src/forge/doctor.py:115-125); the spec does not say how it proves Codex actually loaded and ran the approved deny hook before worker execution.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:38-39 and :105-106 do not define a fail-closed result if the SDK approval-handler replacement cannot be installed or receives an unfamiliar request. The proposed contract test needs to prove an approval request is declined, logged, and cannot execute the requested action.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:45-51 leaves the per-kind settings contract to guesswork: which keys may override the normal Codex stack, how invalid files fail, when settings are reloaded on resume, and whether a kind file may override sandbox or approval policy. The [SDK API](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/sdk/python/docs/api-reference.md) exposes configuration and per-turn policy overrides, so their precedence matters.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:54-61 does not identify the title source for a fix, which has no STORY, or state whether Review, Explore, and Debug are merely naming advice for manually opened threads. Those cases cannot be tested against the stated title format.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:64-74 does not define when the local thread record is durably written or how simultaneous `forge work` calls for one item are serialized. A crash after starting a thread, or two callers resuming the same recorded thread, can lose continuity or run overlapping edits; the current close flow has no worker-running check (src/forge/close.py:39-81).

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:67-69 does not define the baseline for 'commits since the thread's last turn' after a rebase, merge, or amended commit, nor whether untracked files are included in 'uncommitted changes'. The continuation can otherwise omit changes the warm thread has not seen.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:70-81 says an unresumable record starts fresh while a failed or interrupted turn stays resumable, but gives no rule for an unknown terminal state after a lost connection. Starting fresh while the old turn may still be writing conflicts with one worker per item and with review of a settled diff.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:76-79 does not define which event fields are persisted, how duplicate or missing events affect the final status, or how token usage is represented when the SDK omits it. The success measure later depends on those logs (docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:114-121).

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:84-85 does not explicitly bind Grill threads to a read-only sandbox at thread start and turn start, or specify what a failed or interrupted read writes. The current read command checks for changed non-ignored checkout files using a temporary Git index (src/forge/story.py:427-438); 'any file changed' needs an exact boundary and a test for ignored files.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:105-106 specifies unknown fields in stub responses but does not require a real bundled-runtime smoke test of start, name, resume, deny, events, and shutdown. A stub can pass while the shipped SDK and app-server disagree.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:109-110 does not identify the real Forge task, its task scope, or the evidence that ties its first build, second `forge work`, review, CI, and human merge to one thread. Without that proof, criterion 8 can be asserted from a unit test alone.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:114-122 does not define the measurement window, whether legitimate fresh starts and failed rounds enter the continuation denominator, or how missing and zero input-token usage affects the median cache share. The 90% and 80% targets are therefore not reproducible.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:29-31 says each `forge read` call opens a client and runs one turn, but `forge read --amended` only records the amendment (src/forge/story.py:121-126). Running another turn for that form would violate the one-cold-read flow in docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:165-170.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:40-42 says Forge's deny hook enforces task Scope. The shipped hook checks destructive commands, skipped Git hooks, and merges, with no path-scope check (src/forge/deny.py:17-25, src/forge/deny.py:79-105). Scope is supplied to the reviewer instead (src/forge/review.py:134-151), so the claimed enforcement boundary is false.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:48-51 says a task worktree uses its main repository's settings. Forge sync reads and writes `.codex/config.toml` in the checkout passed to it (src/forge/sync.py:181-184, src/forge/sync.py:246-253); the [Codex configuration loader](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs) also loads project configuration for the thread's working tree. The two copies can differ.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:70-74 says a change to the story's approved part starts a fresh worker. The confirmed v1 contract requires a new human approval when that part changes (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:171-176); a fresh thread must not proceed on the unapproved change.

docs/specs/warm-codex-threads.md:87-90 says the plugin is removed from Forge outside history, while its roadmap item still requires hybrid mode, plugin fallback, a lease-held server, turn ledgers, steering, and client upgrade through the old route (plans/roadmap.json:1020-1041). The active roadmap points to this spec and must be reconciled before it can yield a buildable story.
